text:
Alice: Quick PSA — upgraded the JS/TS SDK in the sample-edge app and hit a weird compile-vs-runtime mismatch. TS passes but the deployed edge worker throws on startup.
Alice: Runtime error snippet:
```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'request')
    at createClient (node_modules/redwood-inference/dist/index.js:42:18)
    at eval (edge-worker.js:10:12)
```
Alice: Local Node dev server is fine. Happens only when bundling for edge (esbuild -> Vercel Edge). SDK import looks like `import Redwood from 'redwood-inference'` in the sample-app.
Ben: Do you have the compiled bundle or the generated import? sometimes default import vs namespace import differs depending on `esModuleInterop`/`allowSyntheticDefaultImports`.
Alice: I tried `import * as Redwood from 'redwood-inference'` and it changes the error to a different shape but still fails. TS types showed `createClient<T = unknown>()` so I assumed generics/unknown were fine.
Carla: Can you paste your tsconfig and package.json main/module fields? bundlers + types + runtime interop are often the culprit.
Alice: tsconfig minimal:
```
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2020",
    "module": "ESNext",
    "lib": ["ESNext", "DOM"],
    "esModuleInterop": false,
    "allowSyntheticDefaultImports": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true
  }
}
```
Alice: package.json: "main": "dist/index.cjs.js", "module": "dist/index.esm.js"
Dimitar: sounds like the runtime is picking up the CJS entry but your bundler resolves to ESM, or vice versa. Edge runtimes are picky about `exports`/`module` fields. If the CJS bundle expects `module.exports.default` you'll get undefined when using default import.
Evan: Also note: when generics default to `unknown` the inferred types can be very conservative and sometimes devs add `as any` which masks interop errors. Not the root cause but it complicates debugging.
Ben: Quick repro trick: in your edge bundle, search for `createClient` and inspect the surrounding export object. If it's `exports.createClient = ...` then default import won't work without `interop` wrapper.
Alice: Found it — the ESM build exports `export function createClient...` but the CJS build does `module.exports = { createClient }` and there's no `default`. Using `import { createClient } from 'redwood-inference'` fixes the runtime error.
Carla: OK that's actionable — sample-app should prefer named imports for edge targets or we need to ship a CJS build with `exports.default = createClient` for parity.
sdk-bot: Known issue: SDK build omitted synthetic default for older CJS target when we changed the bundler config (RFC #321). Workaround: use named imports or set `esModuleInterop: true` in your tsconfig. We're tracking a fix.
sdk-bot: Link to tracking ticket: https://internal/rdw/SDK-issue-321 (internal)
Dimitar: Two follow-ups: 1) We should add a test that bundles sample-app with both `esModuleInterop` true/false and verifies the edge runtime import shape. 2) Add an example to the onboarding README showing import patterns for Edge (named import note).
Evan: Related tiny DX quirk — the default retry behavior differs between hosted fetch and the edge polyfilled fetch in the sample because of a subtle env check we do. That caused retries to be skipped in the edge variant and made startup errors noisier. I'll file a separate PR.
Alice: For types: any suggestion to avoid users doing `createClient<any>()` as a workaround? I want to keep types helpful but not break edge.
Carla: Add overloads that preserve the exported function shape without forcing a default export. e.g.
```
export function createClient<T = unknown>(opts: Options<T>): Client<T>
```
and keep `export =` out. Avoid `export default` in the CJS bundle — that mismatch bites consumers w/o interop enabled.
Ben: Also update samples to recommend `esModuleInterop: true` in the quickstart for node users, but add a note for edge that named imports are safest.
Alice: I opened PR #3456 on sample-app that switches imports to named and adds a short note in README about `esModuleInterop` vs edge parity.
Carla: I'll take the SDK build change — will add a CI job that bundles the SDK to both CJS+ESM and verifies default vs named shapes.
Evan: Thanks — can we also add a short test for the generics inference so that `createClient()` without explicit type still returns a usable typed client? small TS assertion in tests.
Alice: Great, that should smooth onboarding. :thumbsup: 
Ben: Filed follow-up issues: RDW-789 (bundle exports), RDW-790 (edge retry parity), RDW-791 (ts typing inference test).
Alice: Marking this thread resolved for the sample-app break — leaving notes in the sample-app PR. Thanks all. :rocket:
